artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A^+ the free semigroup of nonempty words over A. A subset X ⊆ A^+ is a code if for all n, m ≥ 1 and all x_1, …, x_n, x'_1, …, x'_m ∈ X, the equality x_1 x_2 ··· x_n = x'_1 x'_2 ··· x'_m forces n = m and x_i = x'_i for every i. A code X is maximal (over A) if X is not properly contained in any other code over A. A subset P ⊆ A^+ is a prefix code if it is a code such that no element of P is a proper prefix of another element of P. Let α denote the abelianization (commutative image) map, sending each noncommutative formal series over A with nonnegative integer coefficients to its commutative image in the polynomial semiring N[A]; for a language L ⊆ A^+, α(L) denotes the commutative image of its characteristic series. A code X ⊆ A^+ is called commutatively prefix if there exists a prefix code P ⊆ A^+ such that α(X) = α(P).

Question: Is every finite maximal code commutatively prefix?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Perrin and Schützenberger) that every finite maximal code is commutatively equivalent to a prefix code remains open. Only partial results are known; e.g., factorizing codes are known to be commutatively prefix, and recent work (such as the 2022 preprint "Finite maximal codes and factorizations of cyclic groups") establishes further partial cases, but the general problem is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Finite maximal codes and factorizations of cyclic groups
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjecture that every finite maximal code is commutatively equivalent to a prefix code and presents partial results.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open with only partial results known.

status_evidence.title: Constructing Finite Maximal Codes from Schützenberger Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Concerns the Schützenberger conjecture about finite maximal codes and their structure.
status_evidence.claim: The Schützenberger/Perrin conjecture on commutative equivalence of finite maximal codes to prefix codes is a longstanding open problem.
